meta.title: How WPS works | WPS Ranking
meta.description_one: How the WPS score is calculated from official WCA world ranks in {{n}} event, how event weights are chosen, and where the data comes from.
meta.description_other: How the WPS score is calculated from official WCA world ranks in {{n}} events, how event weights are chosen, and where the data comes from.

hero.title: How <hl>WPS</hl> works
hero.text_one: WPS gives every cuber one score from 0 to 100. It is based on their official WCA world ranks in {{n}} event. A high rank in a big event counts more than the same rank in a small one.
hero.text_other: WPS gives every cuber one score from 0 to 100. It is based on their official WCA world ranks in {{n}} events. A high rank in a big event counts more than the same rank in a small one.

formula.title: The formula
formula.step1: For each event, your world rank is compared with the number of people in that event's ranking. World #1 gets the full event weight. Last place gets 0.
formula.step2: The scores of all your events are added up.
formula.step3: The total is divided by the maximum possible score, {{max}}, and multiplied by 100. A WPS of 100 would mean world #1 in every event.
formula.legend: R<sub>e</sub> is your world rank in event e, N<sub>e</sub> is the number of people in that ranking, and w<sub>e</sub> is the event weight. ln is the natural logarithm.
formula.log: The logarithm makes a climb near the top worth more than the same climb near the bottom. In 3x3, going from #20 to #10 adds 0.72 WPS. Going from #20,010 to #20,000 adds less than 0.01 WPS.

measures.title: What WPS measures
measures.does1: How high you rank across all the events you compete in.
measures.does2: Consistency. Most events use the ranking by average, so one lucky solve does not count.
measures.not1: Records or career peaks. WPS uses current ranks.
measures.not2: Strength in one event alone. The world #1 in 3x3 ranks below many all-rounders because they compete in fewer events.
measures.not3: Entering events. A result near the bottom of an event adds almost nothing.

others.title: WPS, Kinch ranks and Sum of Ranks
others.intro: Kinch ranks and Sum of Ranks are two other all-around rankings that cubers use. Each one answers a different question.
others.sorText: Adds up your world ranks in every event. An event without a result counts as last place. Lower is better. Rank #500 in 3x3 counts the same as #500 in 5x5 Blindfolded, although 3x3 has about 250 times as many ranked people.
others.kinchText: Compares your personal record with the world record in each event and averages the scores over all events. A missing event counts as 0. The score depends on how fast the current record holder is.
others.wpsText: Uses world ranks, like Sum of Ranks. Each rank is compared with the number of people in the event, and events with more competitors have a higher weight. A missing event adds 0, like in Kinch ranks.

single.title: Average or single
single.text: Most events use the WCA ranking by average. 3x3, 4x4 and 5x5 Blindfolded, Multi-Blind and Fewest Moves use the ranking by single. In these events most competitors never get an average. An average takes three successful blindfolded solves in one round, and Multi-Blind has no average at all. By single, 3x3 Blindfolded has about three times as many ranked people as by average.

weights.title: Event weights
weights.intro: A weight follows how many people compete in the event. 3x3 has the most competitors and weight 1. 5x5 Blindfolded has the fewest and weight 0.1.

data.title: Data and updates
data.source: Rankings come from the official <link>WCA results export</link>. Every day at 02:00 UTC a job checks for a new export and recalculates all rankings.
data.independent: WPS Ranking is an independent project and is not affiliated with the WCA.
data.notice: This information is based on competition results owned and maintained by the World Cube Association, published at <link>worldcubeassociation.org/results</link>.
data.noticeDated: This information is based on competition results owned and maintained by the World Cube Association, published at <link>worldcubeassociation.org/results</link> as of {{date}}.
data.idea: The idea of a weighted all-around ranking comes from STUCUBE's video <link>When You're The Best In The World But No One Cares</link>. The formula on this site is a modified version.
